question: Which country hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __India__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__** 

__
 
• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 will be the 13th edition of the tournament, and it was held in India in October and November 2023.
 
• The competition will be held fully in India for the first time.
 
• Three earlier events – 1987, 1996, and 2011 – were partially hosted there.
 
• The tournament was originally slated to take place from February 9 through March 26, 2023.
 
• Namibia, along with Zimbabwe and South Africa, will host the Men's Cricket World Cup for the first time in October/November 2027. The event was last held in 2003 in South Africa and Zimbabwe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The Cricket World Cup is a one-day international (ODI) cricket tournament held every four years.
 
• The International Cricket Council (ICC), the sport's governing body, hosts the event every four years, with preliminary qualification stages leading up to a finals competition.
 
• First edition: 1975 - Held in England
 
• Latest edition: 2019 - Held in England & Wales

 
• Current champion - Australia(5 titles)
 
• Most successful - Australia (5 titles)
 
• Most runs - (India) Sachin Tendulkar (2,278).
 
• Most wickets - (Australia) Glenn McGrath (71).
